Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

maintain verb

keep up, keep in good order

also keep up, keep in good repair, maintenance, upkeep

classical

Quint. 1.1.14: cum aequālī cūrā linguam utramque tuērī coeperīmus
Tac. Dial. 28.4: cujus praecipua laus erat tuērī domum

tueor, tuērī, tuitus sum

verb, second conjugation, deponent, transitive

keep up, look after, maintain

Lewis & Short: “to look to, care for, keep up, uphold, maintain, support, guard, preserve, defend, protect” (“the predom. class. signif. of the word”): of a house, a language, a friendship.

Other words

  • servō, servāre, servāvī, servātum — keep, keep up (a state of mind, a custom)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Hor. Carm. 2.3.1–2: aequam mementō rēbus in arduīs servāre mentem

  • retineō, retinēre, retinuī, retentum — keep, hold on to

    verb, second conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.104: lūdendī etiam est quīdam modus retinendus

  • sartum tēctum tuērī — keep (a building) in good repair

    phrase · also used · classical · M-O s.v. maintain (a building); Cic. Fam. 13.50.2: sartum et tēctum, ut ajunt

    The builders’ phrase for upkeep, “patched and roofed”; Cicero uses it as a saying (ut ajunt) of keeping a friend safe and sound.

  • tūtēla, tūtēlae f. — upkeep, care

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 2.17.3: vīlla ūsibus capāx, nōn sūmptuōsa tūtēlā

Examples

  • ita fīet, ut, cum aequālī cūrā linguam utramque tuērī coeperīmus, neutra alterī officiat

    So it will come about that, once we begin to keep up both languages with equal care, neither will get in the way of the other.Quint. 1.1.14

  • aequam mementō rēbus in arduīs servāre mentem

    Remember to keep a level head when things are hard.Hor. Carm. 2.3.1–2

  • vīlla ūsibus capāx, nōn sūmptuōsa tūtēlā

    a house big enough for one’s needs, and not costly to keep upPlin. Ep. 2.17.3

See also provide for, repair, keep, protect.
